subject: biology-2
question: The **taxonomic hierarchy** runs from broad to narrow categories. An organism belongs to the family Felidae; which broader category is the next one up that must also contain it?

options.text: Genus, because families are nested inside genera.
Species, because each family contains many species.
Class, because families sit directly below classes.

explanation: The standard hierarchy runs domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, so the category directly broader than family is order, and any organism in a family is automatically in that order. A and B run the wrong direction, placing the narrower ranks genus and species inside family. C skips a rung, since class is two ranks above family with order between them.
